Chapter 3: The Words We Speak — Shaping Reality Through Encouragement.
You know, words have this strange way of sticking around long after we say them. In the middle of a crisis, what we say—to ourselves and to the people we love—can lift us up or drag us down. Most folks don’t realize just how much power their words hold, especially when everything feels up in the air.
For one family, learning to speak words of encouragement truly changed the course of their journey through tough times.
It didn’t happen all at once. They started small. Instead of fixating on everything going wrong, they looked for little moments of kindness, even if they were brief—a child’s laughter echoing through chaos, a neighbor dropping by unexpectedly, or just sharing a meal together at the end of a long day. Each of these moments became a chance to speak hope.
Phrases like, “We’re going to get through this,” began to replace, “We’ll never make it.” The change was gentle, but over time, it really made a difference.
Then came one of those days where it felt like everything fell apart—the car broke down, the bank account was empty, and tempers were running high. Before, that would’ve led to sharp words and blame. But this time, someone took a breath and said, “Let’s just pause. We’re in this together.” Suddenly, the tension eased, and the family found a way to move forward. It became clear that words could either turn up the heat in a crisis or make room for hope.
Choosing to speak life didn’t mean pretending everything was fine. The family still faced real struggles—addiction, money troubles, illness. But they figured out that you can be honest about pain and still choose to encourage each other. Often, the most powerful words were the ones spoken right in the thick of it. Things like, “I see how hard you’re trying,” or “I’m proud of you for not giving up.” Simple, honest phrases that became lifelines.
And let’s be real—negative self-talk is something almost everyone falls into, especially when life gets rough. This family was no different. There were days when doubt crept in, whispering, “You’re a failure,” or, “Things will never get better.” But as they practiced speaking life—even to themselves—something started to shift. Saying, “I’m doing my best,” or, “Today was hard, but tomorrow’s a new day,” didn’t erase the pain, but it made it a little easier to keep moving forward.
They also discovered how much it mattered to speak life to others. Friends and neighbors who were struggling found comfort in a kind word or just knowing someone was listening. Encouraging someone else became a way to break out of their own pain—it was a reminder that everyone’s fighting their own battles, and a little kindness can go a long way.
Of course, there were setbacks. Old habits don’t disappear overnight, and sometimes harsh words would slip out. But each time, they came back to the practice of encouragement. They apologized when they needed to, and forgave each other’s mistakes. Gradually, their home became a place where hope was spoken aloud, even when life looked bleak.
So, here’s the key takeaway—words spoken in the middle of hardship have the power to shape reality. By choosing to speak life, this family built an environment where healing could actually happen. Their journey wasn’t over, but each day, they faced whatever came next with a little more hope, knowing that the words they chose could make all the difference.
